messages:
Alex: FYI seeing a spike of gRPC streaming stalls affecting long-running training jobs in eu-west-1, pod-to-pod traffic stalls and retries are climbing.
Deepa: which nodes/az? any pattern with GPU pools?
Alex: mostly on gpu-pool-2 (az eu-west-1b). Queue length on scheduling host up 3x. Streaming clients show 'stream recv error: rpc closed' repeatedly.
Sam: can you paste a small log sample + netstat/tcpdump? I want to check if it's TLS or transport.
Alex: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:23Z svc: recv error: rpc closed
2026-03-17T09:12:23Z svc: retrying chunk 42
2026-03-17T09:12:28Z svc: timeout waiting for response frame
```
Also ran tcpdump on a node, saw many fragments and out-of-order reassembly attempts.
Mike: did we recently change CNI mtu or enable encap offload? We rolled vxlan tweaks last week in that region.
Nora: Confirmed: a config flip to enable GSO offload on host interfaces was pushed to eu-west-1b on 3/10. Might interact with VXLAN/GRO.
Alex: packet capture shows lots of IP fragments with DF=0 and reassembly timeouts, gRPC stream waits for full frames -> stall.
Deepa: Could be PMTU mismatch: egress path MTU lower than node/pod believes, causing fragmentation across node-to-node. Any PMTU probes visible?
Sam: ran `ip link` and `ip route` on affected node:
```
ip link show vxlan0 mtu 8950
ip link show eth0 mtu 1500
```
But vxlan0 mtu is high; encap overhead should reduce pod MTU. If overlay and physical mismatched it can fragment.
Nora: kernel dmesg shows reassembly failures and 'GRO: wrong checksum' warnings on some nodes.
infra-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-0423, pager duty alerted. Runbook: cordon nodes, scale down non-critical jobs, collect captures.
Mike: temporary mitigation: set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes and disable tx offload on vxlan interface. That reduced stalls for a small window.
Deepa: we need an actual root fix: either clamp pod MTU in CNI to safe value (e.g., 1400) or ensure underlying path supports 8950+encap. Any cloud uplink MTU logs?
Alex: cloud provider confirms one transit switch in eu-west-1b had MTU 1500 on a peering link to storage fabric — mismatch introduced fragmentation when packets hit that hop.
Sam: proposed immediate action:
- cordon/evacuate pods from affected node batch
- set CNI mtu to 1400 via daemonset for eu-west-1b
- disable GSO on vxlan0 until kernel patch
- monitor gRPC stream success rate
Nora: long-term: update provisioning docs to assert min path MTU >= 9000 for gpu pools and add PMTU checks in node health. Also schedule kernel upgrade on nodes with GRO/GSO fixes.
Alex: rolling out CNI mtU clamp (1400) + disable offload now, starting drain on 4 nodes (job impact small). Will report back in 5m.
Mike: also opening a cost note — job retries burned ~120 GPU minutes in last 2h in that pool, flagging for infra-costs.
Deepa: good, keep me posted. If mitigation holds we'll post a short postmortem and revert the risky encap offload rollout.
Alex: mitigation looks good so far, streams are healthy on drained/updated nodes. Leaving this thread as the timeline / notes.
